title: Gift-planning schedule
html:
Gift-planning schedule

Compute taxable gifts under the supplied exclusions and elections.

Required responses

metadata.taxLawPeriod: 2026; exercise-specific rates and limits are stated in each case

exhibits.title: Cash gifts
exhibits.html: A donor gives $60,000 to each of two recipients as qualifying present interests. Use $19,000 exclusion per donee.

exhibits.title: Other transfers
exhibits.html: Eligible spouses elect gift splitting for a $90,000 present-interest gift to a third recipient. Use $19,000 exclusion per spouse. A separate $25,000 tuition payment directly to a college satisfies the direct-payment exclusion.

explanation:
Taxable gift per first two recipients before credit

$60,000 − $19,000 = $41,000 per recipient.

Combined taxable gifts to the first two recipients

Two × $41,000 = $82,000.

Combined taxable gift after splitting $90,000

Each spouse has $45,000 − $19,000 = $26,000; combined $52,000.

Taxable gift from the qualifying direct tuition payment

The case expressly meets the separate tuition-payment exclusion.
